name: Orbit AI - Phase 1 - Lead intake to Demo Dashboard

nodes.name: Lead intake webhook
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget: acknowledges immediately rather than waiting on both parallel research calls plus the CRM write to finish, since the caller (website form / scraper handoff / manual add) doesn't need that result synchronously.

nodes.name: Normalize lead fields
nodes.notes: UNCONFIRMED field shape - assumes the lead-intake caller posts these exact field names, including websiteUrl (needed by Front Door Audit) and opportunityId (the Twenty CRM record this lead was already created as, per Section 1's 'multi-source intake ... all land in one Opportunity object' - assumes the Opportunity is created before this webhook fires, not by this workflow). No source specifies the real lead form schema yet.

nodes.name: Deep Dive Research
nodes.notes: Deep Dive Research doesn't exist as a built service yet - brief v2 describes it as 'business identity confirmation, web presence audit, review pattern analysis, competitor scan, opening-line recommendation - short brief, not full report,' with no request/output schema specified. This node's assumed response shape ({summary, reportUrl}, referenced downstream) is this workflow's own invention pending the real contract, not something confirmed - flagged, not silently guessed. Per the brief's architecture principle (demo generator = standalone service, not n8n Code nodes), this should most likely be another dedicated Node/TS service.

nodes.name: Front Door Audit
nodes.notes: NEW (brief v2) - 'live scored audit of the lead's actual website + AI-answer-engine readiness across 10 weighted categories (Score -> Rebuild Target -> Point Lift).' Not built anywhere in this repo: the brief names the shape of the output (a score, a rebuild target, a point lift) but not what the 10 categories actually are or how they're weighted - building the real scoring logic now would mean inventing those 10 categories, not encoding a decided set. This node's assumed response shape ({score, rebuildTarget, pointLift, reportUrl}, referenced downstream) is this workflow's own placeholder pending that design work, same flagged-not-guessed treatment as Deep Dive Research above. Runs in PARALLEL with Deep Dive Research per the Launch Checklist's explicit 'parallel Deep Dive Research + Front Door Audit' build step - both branch off the same Normalize node, not chained.

nodes.name: Merge research + audit
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: joins the two parallel branches back into one item before the CRM write, since both results are needed together. The Merge node's parameter names/shape (mode/combineBy) have changed across n8n versions more than most core nodes - this is the single most likely node in this workflow to need hand-fixing on import. If 'combine'/'combineByPosition' isn't right on the real instance, any mode that produces one item per input pair (not multiplied/all-pairs) is the goal.

nodes.name: Write Opportunity to Twenty CRM (stage: Demo Queue)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ stage: 'Demo Queue', dueDiligenceStatus: 'Complete', dueDiligenceReportUrl: $('Deep Dive Research').item.json.reportUrl, frontDoorAuditStatus: 'Complete', frontDoorAuditScore: $('Front Door Audit').item.json.score, frontDoorAuditReportUrl: $('Front Door Audit').item.json.reportUrl }) }}

nodes.notes: Per Section 13's Opportunity Card UX principle - 'a status badge + button opening the actual tool in a new tab, no embedded tools or inline live data inside the CRM itself; it references, it doesn't host' - this writes STATUS FIELDS AND LINK-OUT URLS, not the raw research/audit content. Corrected from an earlier draft of this workflow that dumped the full Deep Dive Research response into a CRM field, which the new CRM Architecture section explicitly rules out. Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as before (confirm field names, and whether 'stage' is a literal string or a select-field option ID, against the real instance).

main.node: Write Opportunity to Twenty CRM (stage: Demo Queue)
